title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: federated connectors can create, update and delete in third-party systems
summary: The briefing passes: the licensing, connector write behaviour, approval controls and five administrator paths are supported. One descriptive claim about what the confirmation card explains is unverified; the briefing should also acknowledge that Microsoft's general connectors overview still contains read-only wording.

claims.where: front matter: status
claims.claim: The roadmap item is launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate
claims.claim: The roadmap target is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "October CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: previewDate

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Federated connectors use Model Context Protocol to access third-party data in real time.
claims.quote: Federated connectors use MCP to access data in real time, so Copilot can retrieve up-to-date information directly from external systems.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Actions use the user's account and source-system permissions, so users can change only what they can already change directly.
claims.quote: Actions run in the third-party service on behalf of the user and are limited by that user's permissions. Copilot can change only what the user is already permitted to change in the source system.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: No data is indexed into Microsoft 365. Copilot sends the connector the information it needs to complete the action and returns the outcome to the user.

claims.where: What's changing: Until October 2026
claims.claim: Federated connectors were read-only before the October 2026 write-actions change.
claims.quote:
Write actions will be available starting early October 2026.

- Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Publisher-provided create, update and delete tools are now usable in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: When a connector provides the appropriate tools, users can ask Microsoft 365 Copilot to create, update, or delete information in a connected third-party system on their behalf.
claims.fix: Add after the first paragraph of What's changing: 'The general Copilot connectors overview still describes federated connectors as read-only, alongside a note that write actions start in early October 2026; this briefing follows the launched roadmap item and the feature-specific federated connectors overview.' The conflicting page is https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview.

claims.where: What's changing: ticket, CRM record and comment examples
claims.claim: Example actions include turning an escalation email into an issue, updating a CRM record and adding a ticket comment without leaving Copilot.
claims.quote: a user can turn an escalation email into an issue in a project-tracking tool, update a record in a customer relationship management (CRM) system, or add a comment to a ticket directly from Copilot Chat.

claims.where: What's changing: The roadmap item says every action
claims.claim: The roadmap says every create, update or delete action requires explicit user confirmation.
claims.quote: every create, update, or delete action requires the user's explicit confirmation before it runs.

claims.where: What's changing: Needs approval
claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools default to Needs approval, which means Copilot asks for confirmation each time.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The confirmation card lets users inspect the action parameters before approving.
claims.quote: Users can expand the card to review the action parameters before approving it.

claims.where: What's changing: nothing is transmitted
claims.claim: While an action awaits confirmation, nothing is sent to the connected system until the user responds.
claims.quote: While an action is awaiting confirmation, nothing is sent to the connected system until the user responds.

claims.where: What's changing: Allow once; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Allow once approves the current action and asks again on the next use of the tool.
claims.quote: Allow once | Runs the action now. Copilot asks again the next time it wants to use the tool.

claims.where: What's changing: Allow for conversation
claims.claim: Allow for conversation suppresses further prompts for that tool during the current conversation.
claims.quote: Allow for conversation | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool for the rest of the current conversation.

claims.where: What's changing: Always allow; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Always allow suppresses future prompts for that user's tool until the user changes its setting or the publisher changes the tool.
claims.quote: Always allow | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool until the user changes the setting or the publisher changes the tool.

claims.where: What's changing: Cancel; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Cancel declines the action and leaves the connected system unchanged.
claims.quote: Cancel | Declines the action. Nothing is changed in the connected system.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls: reusable approvals
claims.claim: Reusable approvals apply to individual tools rather than the whole connector.
claims.quote: Always allow and Allow for conversation apply to the individual tool, not to the whole connector.

claims.where: What's changing: revocable in Settings; Governance controls: Users manage individual tool approvals
claims.claim: Users review or reset approval settings under Copilot Settings > Sources > connector > Tools > Write/Delete tools.
claims.quote: Users can review or reset tool permissions in Copilot by going to Settings > Sources and selecting the connector. The Tools section groups the connector's Write/Delete tools separately from its Read tools.

claims.where: What's changing: publisher adds or changes a tool
claims.claim: A new or changed write-capable tool is set to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to Needs approval by default.

claims.where: What's changing: roadmap administrator tools statement
claims.claim: The roadmap says administrators can view read and write/delete tools in the admin center and disable connectors.
claims.quote: Admins can view each connector's read and write/delete tools in the Microsoft 365 admin center and disable connectors that don't meet their organization's policies.

claims.where: summary; What's changing: Coming soon; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn labels the administrator connector tool-list experience Coming soon.
claims.quote: View a connector's tools in the admin center (Coming soon)

claims.where: What's changing: not available for all connectors; Governance controls
claims.claim: The administrator tool list is not available for every connector.
claims.quote: Viewing tools in the admin center isn't available for all connectors.

claims.where: What's changing: Tools section and All tools; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Where supported, administrators sign in to the third-party service in the connector's Tools section and select All tools.
claims.quote:
On the connector's details page, go to the Tools section and sign in to the third-party service.
3. Select All tools, and then review the list to identify tools that can create, update, or delete data.

claims.where: What's changing: tool list reflects account permissions
claims.claim: The administrator tool list reflects the permissions of the account used to sign in.
claims.quote: The tool list reflects the permissions of the account used to sign in.

claims.where: What's changing: fallback Settings path; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn recommends Copilot Settings > Sources > connector > Write/Delete tools when the administrator view is unavailable.
claims.quote: If you encounter issues, sign in to Microsoft 365 Copilot with your user account, go to Settings -> Sources, and select the connector. Then expand Write/Delete tools.

claims.where: What's changing: supported experiences; Scope
claims.claim: Write-capable federated connectors are supported in Copilot Chat, agents, Cowork and Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
- Agents
- Cowork
- Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook
- Researcher agent

The Researcher agent doesn't support write, update, or delete actions.

claims.where: What's changing: Researcher; Risk assessment; Scope
claims.claim: The Researcher agent remains read-only for federated connectors.
claims.quote: The Researcher agent doesn't support write, update, or delete actions. Federated Copilot connectors remain read-only in this experience.

claims.where: What's changing: default connectors appear as Ready
claims.claim: Microsoft-provided default federated connectors appear as Ready in the admin center connections list.
claims.quote: Default federated connectors are provided by Microsoft and appear as Ready in your connections list in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: What's changing: Admin-published; Scope
claims.claim: Admin-published federated connectors can create, update or delete data where their tools support it, with user approval and source permissions.
claims.quote: Admin-published FCCs can also create, update, or delete data where the connector provides those tools, with the user's approval and subject to their permissions in the source system.

claims.where: What's changing: supported actions vary; Scope
claims.claim: Supported actions vary by admin-published connector.
claims.quote: Supported actions vary by connector.

claims.where: Why it matters: export Customer Data; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft describes write actions as exporting Customer Data to the connected system.
claims.quote: These actions export Customer Data to the connected system to create, update, delete, or otherwise modify data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An action can send conversation content, potentially including Microsoft 365 content, to the third party as its payload.
claims.quote: a user can turn an escalation email into an issue in a project-tracking tool ... These actions export Customer Data to the connected system

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Federated connectors use the user's OAuth connection to the service.
claims.quote: An OAuth-based identity configuration between the external service and Microsoft Entra ID, so Copilot can query the source on behalf of the signed-in user.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity, static egress
claims.claim: MCP servers restricting incoming traffic by source IP must allow Microsoft's static egress addresses.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Copilot selects relevant connector tools dynamically.
claims.quote: When appropriate, Microsoft 365 Copilot dynamically selects relevant tools to retrieve information or perform an action.

claims.where: Risk assessment: no administrator override; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No tenant-wide administrator setting forcing Needs approval is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: federated connectors write actions tenant administrator always require approval DLP government clouds; federated connectors approval administrator always. Opened federated-connectors-overview, manage-federated-connectors and agent-settings; only user-managed approval settings found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Write tools are part of the connector rather than a separate enablement, so enabled read connectors can gain publisher-provided write tools without new admin action.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools are part of the connector and aren't enabled separately. ... The actions available through a connector depend on the tools exposed by the connector publisher. Publishers can add or change tools over time.

claims.where: Why it matters: Purview audit; Governance controls: final sentence
claims.claim: Federated connector activity can be audited in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval. Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support, the card explains this
claims.claim: The confirmation card itself explains that cancelling leaves the third-party system unchanged.
claims.quote: Searched: federated connectors confirmation Cancel card. Opened federated-connectors-overview: its documentation table explains Cancel and its image description names the Cancel button, but neither establishes that the card itself explains the outcome.
claims.fix: Replace 'the card explains this but training helps' with 'training helps'. The documented claim that Cancel leaves the connected system unchanged can remain.
